claims.title: Ewe ancestors present in the region
claims.summary: By oral tradition and scholarly reconstruction, the ancestors of the Ewe had moved into the Togo–Ghana region from the east, settling around Tado and later the town of Notsé before their dispersal.

sources.label: Exodus of the Ewe from Notsé

claims.title: The Ewe exodus from Notsé
claims.summary: Ewe tradition tells of escape from the walled town of Notsé and the tyranny of King Agokoli, after which the people dispersed westward and southward — a foundational narrative of Ewe identity across Ghana, Togo and Benin.

sources.label: Exodus of the Ewe from Notsé

claims.title: Northern peoples and the Batammariba
claims.summary: The Kabye, Tem, Bassar and other groups settled the northern hills, while the Batammariba built the takienta mud tower-houses of the Koutammakou, living in largely decentralised, clan-based communities.

sources.label: Koutammakou, the Land of the Batammariba

claims.title: Founding of Aného (Petit-Popo)
claims.summary: Ane settlers fleeing conflict around Elmina in present-day Ghana founded Aného on the Togolese coast; it grew into the region's chief commercial and slaving port and would later briefly serve as a colonial capital.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-1663-founding-of-aneho-petit-popo, claim TL:TGO:event:1663:founding-of-aneho-petit-popo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Slave Coast and the Atlantic trade
claims.summary: The Togolese shore formed part of the 'Slave Coast', through whose ports including Aného enslaved Africans were trafficked to the Americas — a sustained system of violence and dispossession that reshaped coastal and interior societies.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-1700-the-slave-coast-and-the-atlantic-trade, claim TL:TGO:event:1700:the-slave-coast-and-the-atlantic-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: From slaving to 'legitimate' trade
claims.summary: As the slave trade was suppressed, commerce on the coast turned to palm oil and other goods, and German and other European merchant houses established themselves at Aného and along the shore.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-1850-from-slaving-to-legitimate-trade, claim TL:TGO:event:1850:from-slaving-to-legitimate-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Nachtigal proclaims a protectorate
claims.summary: Gustav Nachtigal signed a protectorate treaty on the coast, associated with a ruler styled Mlapa, declaring German authority over the shore — the founding act of the colony of Togoland.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-1884-nachtigal-proclaims-a-protectorate, claim TL:TGO:event:1884:nachtigal-proclaims-a-protectorate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Berlin Conference recognises Togoland
claims.summary: At the Berlin Conference the European powers laid down rules for partitioning Africa and recognised the German protectorate that became the colony of Togoland.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-1884-the-berlin-conference-recognises-togoland, claim TL:TGO:event:1884:the-berlin-conference-recognises-togoland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Lomé becomes the colonial capital
claims.summary: The seat of German administration moved to Lomé, which grew into the colony's main port and commercial centre, served by railways and roads built across Togoland.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-1897-lome-becomes-the-colonial-capital, claim TL:TGO:event:1897:lome-becomes-the-colonial-capital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: A 'model colony' built on forced labour
claims.summary: Germany promoted Togoland as a profitable Musterkolonie, but its plantations, railways and balanced budget depended on heavy taxation and the coercion of forced African labour.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-1900-a-model-colony-built-on-forced-labour, claim TL:TGO:event:1900:a-model-colony-built-on-forced-labour, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Anglo-French conquest of Togoland
claims.summary: At the start of the First World War, British and French forces invaded German Togoland; after destroying the Kamina wireless station, the German garrison surrendered on 26 August 1914.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-1914-anglo-french-conquest-of-togoland, claim TL:TGO:event:1914:anglo-french-conquest-of-togoland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Partition into British and French mandates
claims.summary: Togoland was divided between Britain and France and formalised by the League of Nations as two mandates — British Togoland in the west and French Togoland in the east — splitting the Ewe and other peoples.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-1922-partition-into-british-and-french-mandates, claim TL:TGO:event:1922:partition-into-british-and-french-mandates, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British Togoland votes to join Ghana
claims.summary: In a UN-supervised plebiscite, about 58 per cent of British Togoland's voters chose union with the Gold Coast; the territory was integrated into Ghana, which became independent in 1957.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-1956-british-togoland-votes-to-join-ghana, claim TL:TGO:event:1956:british-togoland-votes-to-join-ghana, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Olympio's CUT wins the elections
claims.summary: Sylvanus Olympio's nationalist CUT defeated the pro-French parties in the 1958 elections, and Olympio became head of government of the Trust Territory of French Togoland.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-1958-olympio-s-cut-wins-the-elections, claim TL:TGO:event:1958:olympio-s-cut-wins-the-elections, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence of the Republic of Togo
claims.summary: French Togoland became the fully independent Republic of Togo, ending UN trusteeship; the United States recognised the new state the same day, and Olympio was elected its first president in 1961.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Togo

claims.title: Assassination of Sylvanus Olympio
claims.summary: Demobilised soldiers, among them Étienne Gnassingbé Eyadéma, killed President Olympio in Lomé — widely cited as the first military coup against an elected leader in independent sub-Saharan Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-1963-assassination-of-sylvanus-olympio, claim TL:TGO:event:1963:assassination-of-sylvanus-olympio, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Grunitzky installed as president
claims.summary: After the coup, Nicolas Grunitzky, Olympio's brother-in-law and political rival, headed a civilian government, but his weak administration left the military as the country's decisive power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-1963-grunitzky-installed-as-president, claim TL:TGO:event:1963:grunitzky-installed-as-president, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Eyadéma seizes power
claims.summary: Étienne Gnassingbé Eyadéma overthrew President Grunitzky in a bloodless coup and took the presidency, beginning a rule that would last nearly four decades.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-1967-eyadema-seizes-power, claim TL:TGO:event:1967:eyadema-seizes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the RPT one-party state
claims.summary: Eyadéma created the Rassemblement du Peuple Togolais as Togo's sole legal party, the institutional core of his personal autocracy and cult of personality.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-1969-founding-of-the-rpt-one-party-state, claim TL:TGO:event:1969:founding-of-the-rpt-one-party-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Pro-democracy pressure and a new constitution
claims.summary: A wave of unrest forced Eyadéma to accept a multiparty constitution in 1992, but he retained power through disputed elections and the loyalty of the army.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-1992-pro-democracy-pressure-and-a-new-constitution, claim TL:TGO:event:1992:pro-democracy-pressure-and-a-new-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Eyadéma and dynastic succession
claims.summary: Eyadéma died after nearly 38 years in power, then Africa's longest-serving ruler; the army installed his son Faure Gnassingbé, prompting an international outcry over the unconstitutional handover.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-2005-death-of-eyadema-and-dynastic-succession, claim TL:TGO:event:2005:death-of-eyadema-and-dynastic-succession, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Faure Gnassingbé elected amid violence
claims.summary: After ECOWAS pressure forced him to step down, Faure Gnassingbé won a disputed election; the contested result was followed by violence that UN estimates put at hundreds of deaths.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Togo: From the Ewe exodus out of walled Notsé and the mud tower-houses of the Batammariba to the German 'model colony', a partitioned mandate, and a half-century ruled by one family.", terralore.co/country/TGO/chronicle#ev-2005-faure-gnassingbe-elected-amid-violence, claim TL:TGO:event:2005:faure-gnassingbe-elected-amid-violence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
